name: Sanasaryan Han, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Istanbul
positioning: Luxury hotel in an 1895 neo-classical building in the heart of Istanbul's historic Old Town, within walking distance of the Grand Bazaar, Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia
best_for: Travelers who want to explore Istanbul's Old Town landmarks on foot
Guests drawn to history, books, art and Turkish tea and sweet-making traditions
Cruise travelers starting or ending a voyage at Galataport Istanbul

facts.text: The building was built in 1895 in a neo-classical style.
It was designed by Ottoman architect Hovsep Aznavur and commissioned by philanthropist Migirdiç Sanasaryan.
The han was once an office building whose rents were all paid into a foundation for the Sanasaryan School.
The hotel is in the heart of Istanbul's historic Old Town.
The Spice Bazaar, Grand Bazaar, Blue Mosque, Hagia Sophia and Karaköy are within walking distance.
The hotel is minutes from Galataport Istanbul and its international cruise terminal.
The walls display monochromatic photographs of Istanbul by photographer Harun Doğan.
Rooms have high ceilings, and beds have Turkish motifs and Frette linens.
Every room has a Turkish tea set with the hotel's own tea blends, served in traditional glass cups and copper plates.
The Sanasaryan Han Suite's Atrium Living room has views of old Istanbul.
Siran Restaurant offers a seven-stage tasting menu paired with local wines.
Siran Terrace serves contemporary cuisine and signature beverages in a garden setting.

highlights.text: Honouring its heritage as a beacon of education, the hotel displays a curated collection of artifacts and antique books.
A grand chandelier takes centre stage in the hotel's light-bathed atrium.
Every day a dedicated Tea Master explains the origins and characteristics of tea leaves.
Guests get a weekly invitation to make their own clotted cream Turkish delight at the Hacı Bekir atelier, steps from the hotel.
Rooms have marble bathrooms with handmade copper trays and traditional hammam bowls inspired by the Turkish bath ritual.

considerations.text: The hotel does not offer on-site parking.
WhataHotel notes the tourist area can be crowded during peak seasons.
